title: Aphorism § 199
text:
§ 199



 If the remedy perfectly homoeopathic to the disease had not yet
          been discovered 1  at the time when the local symptoms were destroyed
          by a corrosive or desiccative external remedy or by the knife, then the case becomes much
          more difficult on account of the too indefinite (uncharacteristic) and inconstant
          appearance of the remaining symptoms; for what might have contributed most to determine
          the selection of the most suitable remedy, and its internal employment until the disease
          should have been completely annihilated, namely, the external principal symptom, has been
          removed from our observation.



1  As was the case before my time with the remedies for the
          condylomatous disease (and the antipsoric medicines).
